error.signature: AI tells a Saudi Arabia tourist e-visa applicant that travel health insurance is optional or must be purchased separately

verdict.summary: Saudi Arabia's tourist e-visa fee (about SAR 535) automatically bundles a government-run visitor health insurance policy administered by the Council of Health Insurance (CHI), covering medical emergencies up to SAR 100,000 and emergency childbirth up to SAR 5,000; there is no way to opt out or buy the visa without it. That basic coverage is bare-bones and does not carry over to a visa extension - CHI requires a fresh insurance policy be issued and linked to the passport for the extension period.

dead_ends.action: Tell a tourist e-visa applicant to shop for or purchase a separate travel health insurance policy to satisfy Saudi Arabia's visa insurance requirement
dead_ends.why_fails: The Council of Health Insurance (CHI)-administered visitor policy is automatically bundled into the roughly SAR 535 e-visa fee and issued digitally alongside the visa; applicants cannot opt out of it or substitute a different policy to get the e-visa issued, though they may add supplementary private coverage on top.
dead_ends.condition: Applying for the Saudi tourist e-visa
dead_ends.common_misconception: That Saudi Arabia's visa insurance works like a checkbox add-on travelers can decline the way they can on many airline booking flows.

dead_ends.action: Assume the original e-visa's bundled insurance automatically extends its coverage if the visit visa itself is extended
dead_ends.why_fails: CHI's guidance states a visitor who extends their visit visa after its expiry must obtain a new insurance policy covering the extension period, linked to their passport - the original bundled policy does not roll over automatically.
dead_ends.condition: Visa extension requested after original expiry

workarounds.action: Apply for the e-visa as normal - the visitor insurance is issued automatically with it - and verify coverage afterward on the CHI website using the visa or passport number
workarounds.how: Use CHI's online insurance-inquiry service (chi.gov.sa) with your visa/passport number to confirm the policy is active before travel.

workarounds.action: If extending a visit visa past its original expiry, arrange a new CHI-linked insurance policy for the extension period through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' Enjaz platform before the extension is finalized

frequently_confused_with.distinction: That canon covers e-visa eligibility and application; this one covers the mandatory, bundled health insurance that comes with it and its extension rules.
